title: Can a lift explain all ten rules?
description: The five rules for adding and the five rules for subtracting in the book are each explained as a movement of the lift between floors. Addition is starting floor plus movement, and subtraction is the movement from one floor to another. The video breaks the slip of thinking that subtraction is a separate idea with no picture.
teaching_notes: One idea: every rule is a movement of the lift, with starting floor plus movement giving the target floor. Watch for students who memorise the rules without seeing the movement, especially for taking away a negative number.

video_script.why: The child explains each addition rule and each subtraction rule as the movement of a lift between floors.
video_script.substitution: The lift of the book: Starting Position + Movement = Target Position, and Target Position − Starting Position = Movement, with the book's own example of each rule.
video_script.anchor: the lift of the book beside its floors, from below the ground to above it
video_script.payoff_line: Every rule is a movement of the lift

final_answer.value: Open-ended: each of the 5 addition rules and 5 subtraction rules is a movement of the lift
final_answer.spoken: each of the ten rules is a movement of the lift

names.{{NAME_8}}: the Indian mathematician who gave rules for adding and subtracting positive numbers, negative numbers and zero in 628 CE

hold_back: Answer: every rule is a movement of the lift
never_show: the claim that the rules cannot be pictured
maths_rules: addition rule 1: 2 + 3 = 5; start on floor 2, go up 3, reach floor 5
addition rule 2: (−2) + (−3) = −5; start on floor −2, go down 3, reach floor −5
subtraction rule 1: 3 − 2 = 1, the movement from floor 2 up to floor 3
subtraction rule 2: 2 − 3 = −1, the movement from floor 3 down to floor 2
subtraction rule 3: 2 − (−3) = 2 + 3 = 5, the movement from floor −3 up to floor 2
subtraction rule 5: −2 − 0 = −2; 0 − (−2) = 2, the movement from floor −2 up to floor 0
video_script.design: One lift shaft with floors from −5 to 5. Each rule is shown as the lift starting on a floor and moving, with arrows in teal for up and amber for down.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the rules of {{NAME_8}}.
<bookmark mark='rules'/>There are five rules for adding and five for subtracting.
<bookmark mark='lift'/>The book asks us to explain them with the lift, or with a number line.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can a lift explain every one of the ten rules?

narration: <bookmark mark='lift'/>In the lift, the starting floor plus the movement gives the target floor.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>The target floor minus the starting floor gives the movement.
<bookmark mark='dir'/>A positive press goes up, and a negative press goes down.
<bookmark mark='inv'/>The number that gives zero when added is called the additive inverse.

marks.given: the word Given is written with the two rows of rule cards

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five rules for adding and five rules for subtracting, with an example of each.

beats.on_screen: To find: each rule explained as a movement of the lift

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to explain each rule as a movement of the lift.

beats.on_screen: rule 1: 2 + 3 = 5, start on floor 2, up 3, reach floor 5; rule 2: (−2) + (−3) = −5, start on floor −2, down 3, reach floor −5

marks.r1: the lift starts on floor 2 and the plus press 3 is chosen
marks.up: the lift goes up 3 floors and 5 appears on the target floor
marks.r2: the lift starts on floor −2 and the press −3 is chosen
marks.down: the lift goes down 3 floors and −5 appears on the target floor
marks.r2b: the sizes 2 and 3 are added without signs and the minus is kept

beats.moves_through: the lift goes up three floors, then down three floors
narration: <bookmark mark='r1'/>Step one, take two positives, two and three.
<bookmark mark='up'/>The lift starts on floor two and goes up three floors, so it reaches floor five.
<bookmark mark='r2'/>Next, take two negatives, minus two and minus three.
<bookmark mark='down'/>The lift starts on floor minus two and goes down three floors to minus five.
<bookmark mark='r2b'/>Add the sizes without signs and keep the minus.

beats.on_screen: rule 3, different signs: −5 + 3 = −2; 2 + (−3) = −1; −3 + 5 = 2; take the smaller size from the greater and keep the sign of the greater

marks.r3: an up arrow and a down arrow pull against each other beside the lift
marks.ex1: the lift starts on floor −5 and goes up 3 floors to −2
marks.ex2: 2 + (−3) = −1 and −3 + 5 = 2 are written beside two short lift paths
marks.rule3: the rule take the smaller size from the greater and keep the sign of the greater is written

beats.moves_through: the lift goes up from floor −5 to floor −2
narration: <bookmark mark='r3'/>Step two, a positive and a negative pull against each other.
<bookmark mark='ex1'/>Minus five plus three: start on floor minus five and go up three floors to minus two.
<bookmark mark='ex2'/>Two plus minus three ends on floor minus one, and minus three plus five ends on floor two.
<bookmark mark='rule3'/>Take the smaller size from the greater, and keep the sign of the greater.

beats.on_screen: rule 4: 2 + (−2) = 0, up 2 and down 2 bring the lift back to the start; rule 5: −2 + 0 = −2, a movement of 0 keeps the lift where it is

marks.r4: the lift goes up 2 floors and then down 2 floors back to its start
marks.inv: the words a number and its additive inverse add to 0 are written
marks.r5: the lift stays on floor −2 and −2 + 0 = −2 is written

beats.moves_through: the lift goes up two floors and then down two floors
narration: <bookmark mark='r4'/>Step three, up two floors and down two floors bring the lift back to the start.
<bookmark mark='inv'/>A number and its additive inverse always add to zero.
<bookmark mark='r5'/>Pressing nothing is a movement of zero, so minus two plus zero stays minus two.

beats.on_screen: subtraction: Target − Starting = Movement; rule 1: 3 − 2 = 1, from floor 2 up to floor 3; rule 2: 2 − 3 = −1, from floor 3 down to floor 2

marks.s1: the rule Target Floor − Starting Floor = Movement is written again
marks.ex1: an arrow goes from floor 2 up to floor 3 and 3 − 2 = 1 is written
marks.ex2: an arrow goes from floor 3 down to floor 2 and 2 − 3 = −1 is written

beats.moves_through: the lift goes up from floor 2 to floor 3, then down again
narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step four, subtraction is the movement from the second floor to the first.
<bookmark mark='ex1'/>Three take away two moves the lift from floor two up to floor three.
That is plus one.
<bookmark mark='ex2'/>Two take away three moves the lift from floor three down to floor two.
That is minus one.

beats.on_screen: rule 3: 2 − (−3) = 5, from floor −3 up to floor 2, the same as 2 + 3; rule 4: 2 − 2 = 0 and (−2) − (−2) = 0; rule 5: −2 − 0 = −2 and 0 − (−2) = 2

marks.s3: an arrow goes from floor −3 up to floor 2 and 2 − (−3) = 5 is written
marks.s4: the lift stays on the same floor and 2 − 2 = 0 is written
marks.s5: −2 − 0 = −2 is written, then an arrow goes from floor −2 up to floor 0 and 0 − (−2) = 2 is written
marks.inv: the movement 2 is labelled the additive inverse of −2

beats.moves_through: the lift goes up from floor −3 to floor 2, then from floor −2 to floor 0
narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step five, take away a negative number.
Two take away minus three moves the lift from floor minus three up to floor two.
<bookmark mark='same'/>That is five floors up, the same as two plus three.
<bookmark mark='s4'/>Taking a number from itself needs no movement, so the answer is zero.
<bookmark mark='s5'/>Minus two take away zero stays minus two.
Zero take away minus two moves the lift from floor minus two up to floor zero.
<bookmark mark='inv'/>That movement is two, the additive inverse of minus two.

marks.check: the rule Starting Floor + Movement = Target Floor is written

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step six, check by adding each movement back to its starting floor.
<bookmark mark='c1'/>Minus three plus five lands on floor two, which matches.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Three plus minus one lands on floor two, which matches too.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Every rule is a movement of the lift.
